title: Parallel Universes: Two Captures, One Mating Rank
summary: After either capture of the queen offer, keep checking on the back rank instead of retreating.

nodes.question: The rook took the queen on f3. What is White’s forcing reply?
nodes.explanation: Re7 can check along the eighth rank. Black’s queen must interpose on c8 because a7 and b7 remain occupied.

nodes.question: The queen took on f3 instead. Does that change the plan?
nodes.explanation: The same Re8 check works, but now Black’s rook must interpose on c8 instead of its queen.

branches.title: Source rook capture: force the queen onto c8
commentary: Begin at the complete seven-piece diagram after ...Rxf3. The earlier eight-piece Qf3 offer and all other defenses remain outside exact verification.
Re8+ is the only winning move in this exact root. It checks along the back rank while Black’s pawns occupy a7 and b7.
Qc8 is Black’s only legal reply. The queen must block the checking rook’s line to Ka8.
Rxc8# removes the interposing queen with actual mate. The remaining black rook cannot answer the back-rank check, and a7/b7 still block the king’s flights.
branches.explanation: Rxc8# removes the interposing queen with actual mate. The remaining black rook cannot answer the back-rank check, and a7/b7 still block the king’s flights.

branches.title: Source queen capture: force the rook onto c8
commentary: Switch to the separate complete seven-piece diagram after ...Qxf3. This is the alternative capture, not a continuation of the rook-capture branch.
Re8+ again supplies the only winning move. The queen on f3 cannot interpose on the checking segment between e8 and a8.
Rc8 is Black’s only legal reply. The rook on c3 must return to the back rank.
Rxc8# captures the blocking rook. Black’s queen survives, but cannot capture the mating rook or free an occupied flight square.
branches.explanation: Rxc8# captures the blocking rook. Black’s queen survives, but cannot capture the mating rook or free an occupied flight square.

branches.title: Independent error: retreat instead of checking
commentary: Independently compare a rook retreat after ...Rxf3. This error is not attributed to the source.
Re1 gives up the forced mate and loses with best play. The queen and rook are allowed to coordinate against White’s exposed king.
Rf2+ is a representative winning check along the second rank. White no longer has the immediate Re8/Qc8/Rxc8 mating sequence.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Rf2+ is a representative winning check along the second rank. White no longer has the immediate Re8/Qc8/Rxc8 mating sequence.

branches.title: Independent error after the queen capture
commentary: Independently compare the same retreat after ...Qxf3, preserving Black’s c3 rook and both pawns.
Re1 again changes a forced win into a forced loss. Giving up the checking tempo lets Black use its material.
Qf2+ checks along the second rank. This is one representative winning reply; the line stops at an exactly checked White loss.

exercises.prompt: Why can the queen not save Black after Qc8?
exercises.answer: It only postpones the check for one move. Rxc8 removes the blocker, while a7 and b7 still occupy the king’s escape squares.

exercises.prompt: Why does a surviving queen not prevent mate?
exercises.answer: The queen on f3 cannot reach c8 or block the rook’s back-rank checking line after Rxc8. Legal defensive moves matter more than material count.

startContext: Two separately illustrated seven-piece roots are checked: after ...Rxf3 at 131 seconds and after ...Qxf3 at 139 seconds. The first frame contains a capture overlay, confirmed by the next settled Re8 diagram; both full positions are preserved. The initial nine-piece setup, later eight-piece Qf3 offer, Qc8 refusal and other source defenses remain outside verification. These lines prove what happens after the two selected captures, not the full sacrifice.
